entry.label: Systemic Intervention
entry.description: Systemic Intervention combines critical reflection on boundaries with methodological pluralism and action. It treats intervention choices as practical, political and ethical rather than technically neutral.
entry.canonical_definition: A systemic methodology that begins with critical reflection on boundaries and values, then draws on methodological pluralism to support responsible action in complex situations.

profile.title: Systemic Intervention
profile.canonical_definition: A systemic methodology that begins with critical reflection on boundaries and values, then draws on methodological pluralism to support responsible action in complex situations.
profile.summary: Systemic Intervention refuses the idea that the problem and method are already given. It asks how boundaries and values create marginalisation, then selects and combines methods in relation to the situation.
profile.why_it_matters: Method choice is itself an intervention. Boundary critique helps practitioners see whose concerns, knowledge and consequences are being made central or peripheral.
practice_connections: record consequences and revise the intervention
common_misreadings: use several methods and call it systemic
the practitioner is outside the intervention
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Named editorial review is still required before canonical acceptance.
